The Ratchet and Clank series is one of the best things that happened to my childhood, and is plenty well able to hold up today. Its cartoony art style means that its early-years PS2 graphics aren't too much of a bother, and they still hold some serious charm. The humour largely went over my head as a kid a lot of the time, so there's definitely a nice range there. The story is fairly straightforward with a couple twists here and there, but it's still pretty compelling - maybe because it's easy to follow, but well written. The level design is all great - very thematic, designed with care and all with a unique style that implants itself in your memory.
But let's get to what Ratchet and Clank is really about: Weapon variety. Insomniac can't get enough of making weird ways to fight enemies. Of course you have your regular pistol thing, a flamethrower, a bomb lobbing glove, a rocket launcher... a rocket-powered punching glove... a lightning gun... a gun that morphs things into sheep..... a gun that sucks enemies and objects in and spits them back out as ammo....... and that's just in the first game! 3 had an amazing variety, with the pseudo liquid physics of the lava/liquid nitrogen gun, the satisfying melee of the quantum whip, or the rift inducer which skipped straight to the point and created miniature black holes.

Right let's forget about the recent ones for the moment (please don't hit me, I'll acknowledge then later).

UFO: Enemy Unknown (a.k.a. X-COM: UFO Defense) The entry level first of the series. Don't let the crummy graphics fool you this game was a thrilling TBS which had you genuinely kacking your pants wondering where the hell that alien activity was. With a great story line and fantastically written documents on weapons, aliens and general history it was just great.

You built your base or bases around the globe, researches your weapons, armor and better equipment and worked to destroy the alien menace. Also the top difficulty modes were high impossible and very unforgiving to even the slightest mistakes.

X-COM: Terror from the Deep Think the first one only with the aliens coming from the ocean. Same great gameplay, research tree and more story content. p.s. Fuck Lobster Men!

X-COM: Apocalypse Took a slightly different route but kept the same TBS and RTS (base construction/research) view as the first two games. Set instead in a city rather than a world wide scale and based on conflicting mega corporations fighting for power.

X-COM: Interceptor The only one I've yet to sit down and play properly but they took a different view on this creation and it's not the most popular of the genre

XCOM: Enemy Unknown ; The Bureau: XCOM Declassified ; XCOM 2 (upcoming) They did a reboot of the series with up to date graphics, key plot characters and slightly altered story line but for old fans and newly indoctrinated folks to the genre these were a resounding success with the new sequel set for the end of this year. This added a multiplayer aspect to the games besides giving additional back story and I've yet to here a bad word about it.

You can pick up all the X-Com games from Steam for €15 for the originals and around €40 for the latest releases. That might be a bit much but these games are fantastic so even if you keep and eye out next Steam Sale they always are on offer.

I would say give Final Fantasy a chance. I know it's not for everyone but in a lot of the games (Final Fantasy 10, 7, and 12 to me especially) a whole new world is introduced and to me it really makes you feel about the places you're in. I feel like a lot of what I like about the series may be coming from nostalgia but through all the great games out there when I want to explore a new world or play a video game that excels at storytelling it's always a final Fantasy game I pick up.

As an end note I do want to stress there are some Final Fantasy games that aren't as fun as the others so it's always a good idea to get opinions on where to start. My recommendation would be Final Fantasy X because it just got a remaster which may make it easier visually as opposed to one of the top down Final Fantasies.
